summary.title: lmbench: Portable tools for performance analysis
summary.one_liner: lmbench is a micro-benchmark suite for measuring basic system building blocks, and the paper describes how its tests were derived from real customer performance problems.
keywords: how to measure memory bandwidth and latency
takeaways: lmbench is a micro-benchmark suite targeting basic building blocks such as memory, system calls, pipes and sockets.
Individual tests were derived from analysis and isolation of real customer performance problems.
The suite has been used to compare system implementations from different vendors and to uncover bugs and design flaws.
The authors report a strong correlation between memory system performance and overall performance.
lmbench includes an extensible database of results from systems current as of late 1995.
summary.summary: This USENIX 1996 paper by Larry McVoy and Carl Staelin introduces lmbench, a portable micro-benchmark suite for measuring the basic building blocks of common applications such as databases, simulations, and networking. The abstract states that each test was built from isolating a real customer performance problem, and that the tools are used to compare systems from different vendors. The authors report that the benchmarks found previously unknown bugs and design flaws and showed a strong link between memory system performance and overall performance. The page text provided is only the abstract and download links, so details of the individual tests and their methodology are not included here.
